title: Open Problem: Finding a Shortest Even Hole
statement_text: Find, in polynomial time, a shortest even hole in a graph (if one exists).
context_text: A hole in a graph is an induced cycle of length at least four; it is even or odd according to the parity of its length (number of edges), and $|G|$ denotes the number of vertices. For odd holes, polynomial algorithms are known to detect an odd hole ($O(|G|^9)$ by Chudnovsky, Scott, Seymour and Spirkl, improved to $O(|G|^8)$ by Lai, Lu and Thorup), to detect an odd hole of length at least $\ell$ for fixed $\ell$, and to find a shortest odd hole in time $O(|G|^{14})$ (Chudnovsky, Scott and Seymour). For even holes, detection is polynomial (Conforti, Cornuéjols, Kapoor and Vušković; Chudnovsky, Kawarabayashi and Seymour; Chang and Lu; $O(|G|^9)$ by Lai, Lu and Thorup), and this paper gives a polynomial algorithm to detect an even hole of length at least $\ell$ for every fixed $\ell$. The remaining analogue, finding a shortest even hole if there is one, the authors have not been able to solve.
notes: Stated informally in the introduction without a labelled environment.

title: Open Question: Detecting Holes of Length Divisible by Three
statement_text: Can holes whose length is a multiple of three be detected in polynomial time?
context_text: A hole in a graph is an induced cycle of length at least four; it is even or odd according to the parity of its length (number of edges), and $|G|$ denotes the number of vertices. Polynomial-time algorithms are known for detecting odd holes, even holes, long odd holes and (by this paper) even holes of length at least any fixed $\ell$. On the other hand, a result of Hajebi (private communication) shows that when $\ell$ is part of the input, detecting a hole of length at least $\ell$ in a prescribed residue class modulo a fixed $m\ge2$ is W[1]-hard. The authors remark that even versus odd has been almost the entire focus of previous research, and ask about holes whose length is a multiple of three: triangle-free graphs with no such hole have very interesting structural properties, but the authors currently have no idea how to recognize such graphs.
notes: Stated informally in the introduction as a rhetorical open question; no labelled environment.
